title: Soften People's Resistance by Confirming Their Self-Opinion: The Law of Defensiveness

chapterBreakdown.gentle: The chapter on defensiveness stays useful because it names a pattern people often feel before they can explain it. This law argues that direct attacks on identity produce resistance faster than truth can land, so influence works best when it confirms a person's self-opinion before trying to move behavior or belief. This is why indirect influence works better. If you confirm some part of how people want to see themselves, resistance softens and curiosity has space to return. The law is therefore less about rhetorical cleverness than about understanding the emotional structure of persuasion. The practical move is to lower ego threat. Let people save face, begin from what they already value about themselves, and guide rather than corner. In conflict, this can mean asking, reframing, inviting ownership, or sequencing truth so the other person can keep dignity while changing. Persuasion should preserve dignity without abandoning reality. That softer honesty is already a practical advantage.
